questions.q: Which job in your pipeline is missing?
questions.hint: A pipeline has four jobs: ingest, store, transform and orchestrate. Most tools only do one.

options.label: Copying data in from databases or apps
options.why: you need to copy data in, and the post's table lists dbt, Airflow, Dagster and Prefect as transform or scheduling tools

options.label: Reshaping data that is already in a warehouse
options.why: your data has landed and needs reshaping, and the post's table lists these tools' main job as ingest or scheduling

options.label: Running the steps in order and retrying failures
options.why: you need something to run the steps in order, and the post's table lists these tools' main job as ingest or transform

options.label: All of it, from one vendor
options.why: you want several jobs from one vendor, and the post lists Matillion, AWS Glue and Azure Data Factory as the bundles

questions.hint: Free software still has a bill: servers and people.

options.label: A vendor runs it for us
options.why: you want someone else to run it

options.label: We run it ourselves, on our own servers
options.why: you want to self-host, and AWS Glue runs only on AWS

questions.q: How fast must changes show up?

options.label: Every few minutes
options.why: you need syncs every few minutes

options.label: Within seconds
options.why: you need seconds, and the post points seconds to Debezium, Kafka and Flink, which you run yourself

options.label: Everything is on AWS
options.why: your data and skills are on AWS

options.label: In a cloud warehouse such as Snowflake or BigQuery
options.why: you work inside a cloud warehouse

options.label: Not tied to one cloud
options.why: you want to stay cloud-neutral, and AWS Glue runs only on AWS

questions.q: What kind of bill do you want?
questions.hint: Rows, events, credits, models and compute hours all grow in different ways.

options.label: Free software, and we pay in staff time
options.why: you prefer free software over a licence bill

options.label: A public price I can plan around
options.why: you need a public price, and Matillion's pricing page shows no dollar price

options.label: I will pay for hands-off loading
options.why: you will budget for hands-off loading

fivetran.name: Fivetran
fivetran.summary: A managed loader with a free plan, 700+ connectors and 15-minute syncs on Standard.
fivetran.bestWhen: You want someone else to run loading and you can budget for the meter.
fivetran.watchOut: Paid rates sit in a separate table and each connection has its own curve, so you need rows per connection to predict a bill, and deleted rows count as paid rows.

airbyte.name: Airbyte
airbyte.summary: A long connector list with a free self-hosted core or a paid cloud.
airbyte.bestWhen: You want lots of connectors and can live with minutes to an hour of delay.
airbyte.watchOut: It is not a continuous streaming tool, and the core uses the Elastic License 2.0, which stops you offering it to others as a managed service.

debezium.name: Debezium
debezium.summary: Free and open source. Its docs say it records database changes as events, and describe delay in the millisecond range for MySQL and PostgreSQL (the project's claim, not a measurement).
debezium.bestWhen: You already run Kafka or have engineers to spare, and need changes in seconds.
debezium.watchOut: It only captures changes. You still need a place to send them and someone to keep it healthy.

matillion.name: Matillion
matillion.summary: One tool for loading, transforming and scheduling inside a cloud warehouse.
matillion.bestWhen: You want one vendor for load and transform on a warehouse.
matillion.watchOut: No dollar price is shown on its pricing page, and we found no Apache Iceberg destination in its docs.

glue.name: AWS Glue
glue.summary: A managed Spark service on AWS with a built-in data catalog, billed by compute time.
glue.bestWhen: Your data and skills already live on AWS.
glue.watchOut: You write Spark code or compose jobs in Glue's visual editor, and it runs only on AWS.

adf.name: Azure Data Factory
adf.summary: A managed Microsoft service for ETL, ELT and data integration.
adf.bestWhen: You live on Azure and run batch jobs.
adf.watchOut: Pipelines are batch only, and Microsoft says new users should start with Fabric Data Factory.

dbt.name: dbt
dbt.summary: Reshapes data already in your warehouse using SQL, with a free plan and open-source core.
dbt.bestWhen: Analysts will write the transformations in SQL.
dbt.watchOut: It does not extract or load anything, so you need a loader first.

airflow.name: Apache Airflow
airflow.summary: A free, code-first scheduler that runs your pipeline steps in order.
airflow.bestWhen: Your team writes Python and wants a free scheduler.
airflow.watchOut: It does not copy data itself, it is built for batch rather than streaming, and you pay for servers and staff.

hevo.name: Hevo
hevo.summary: A managed, no-code loader into a warehouse, with a free plan up to 1M events a month.
hevo.bestWhen: You are a small team that wants a warehouse fed without writing code.
hevo.watchOut: Every insert, update or delete is an event, so busy tables use the quota fast. Streaming sits on higher plans.

dagster.name: Dagster
dagster.summary: A code-first orchestrator that shows your pipeline as the datasets it makes, with built-in lineage.
dagster.bestWhen: You like to see your pipeline as tables and assets rather than tasks.
dagster.watchOut: Each asset run or op is a credit, so many small runs add up. The cheaper plans allow only 1 or 3 users.

prefect.name: Prefect
prefect.summary: An open-source engine that turns plain Python functions into pipelines, with a free Hobby plan.
prefect.bestWhen: Your team already writes Python and wants to start with ordinary functions.
prefect.watchOut: It is code only, and the free plan caps at 5 deployments and 7 days of history.

olake.name: OLake Go
olake.summary: Open-source tool that captures Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB, MongoDB and SQL Server changes into Iceberg or Parquet (Oracle, Db2, S3 and Kafka load without database change capture).
olake.bestWhen: Your sources are databases and you want Iceberg or Parquet on storage you run.
olake.watchOut: Its output is Iceberg and Parquet, so it suits teams that want one of those on storage they run.
